definition: to prove more powerful or become widespread
memoryTip: Pre-vail: come out on top — the stronger side wins.
correctPassage: Despite early resistance, the reform proposal eventually prevailed in the full assembly vote.
wrongPassages: The minority view will prevail only if it is ignored by every decision-maker present.
Calm will prevail in the chamber once shouting drowns out every other voice.
She hoped to prevail the draft by hiding it in a folder no one would open.

memoryTip: Re-pudiate: push it away — “I won’t own that claim.”
correctPassage: The board voted to repudiate the earlier statement once new evidence contradicted it.
wrongPassages: Leaders moved to repudiate the findings by endorsing every recommendation at once.
She repudiated the gift by accepting it with thanks and putting it on display.
The treaty was repudiated only in the sense that both sides rushed to ratify it.

memoryTip: A stone buttress props up a wall — so it supports an argument too.
correctPassage: Fresh survey data buttress the claim that turnout rose most in urban precincts.
wrongPassages: Critics hoped to buttress her thesis by removing the only sources that confirmed it.
The leak will buttress confidence in the system by exposing every security flaw at once.
He tried to buttress the weak beam by cutting away half of its remaining support.

memoryTip: Miti-gate: open a gate to let pressure out — ease the harm.
correctPassage: Cooling stations were set up to mitigate heat risk for outdoor workers during the wave.
wrongPassages: The new rule will mitigate harm by stripping safety checks and raising exposure limits.
They mitigated the shortage by destroying the remaining inventory overnight.
To mitigate traffic, officials closed every alternate route into the city center.

memoryTip: Con-strain: keep under strain — squeezed inside tight limits.
correctPassage: Scarce laboratory space will constrain how many samples the team can process each week.
wrongPassages: Unlimited grants will constrain the lab by removing every budget ceiling at once.
The open border policy was designed to constrain free movement of goods and people.
She hoped to constrain creativity by handing artists a blank canvas and no rules.
